rows.text: It represents an anticipatory-loss or impending-reduction signal. Activity stays elevated while something held is projected to shrink, then relaxes exponentially at rate 0.7 once the projection is resolved.

It represents a stochastic burst or Poisson-style event source. It produces irregular short bursts separated by quiet intervals, and turning the knob increases the burst rate so quiet stretches shorten.
It represents an opaque registry entry or named symbol. The registry records only an identifier and no other field, so its behavior is not exposed here.
It represents a missing-connection alarm with damped oscillatory recovery. Activity follows loss of a long-standing link and returns in decaying waves until the link is re-mapped.
It represents a ternary lookup/composite key. As a key it maps to a list of exactly three other glyphs, with no other recorded metadata.

It represents an invariant or consistency-preservation activity. It persists while system parts remain mutually consistent and belongs to a non-decaying “immortal” class, so it does not fade on its own.
It represents a deformation/strain response. It tracks a running process being forced out of its normal shape and decays exponentially after the shape is restored.
It represents a ternary lookup/composite key. It is a key whose value is a three-glyph list, with no other registry field recorded.
It represents an opaque registry entry or named symbol. Only its identifier is recorded, so no additional fields or behavior are shown.
It represents hysteresis or a Schmitt-trigger switch. Turning the knob up switches the output at one threshold, while turning it back down switches only at a lower threshold.
It represents an opaque registry entry or named symbol. The registry shows only an identifier and no other field.
It represents a bifurcation into bistability, such as a pitchfork bifurcation. As the control knob changes slowly, one stable resting level splits into two possible stable levels.
It represents an opaque registry entry or named symbol. Its only recorded information is an identifier.
It represents a goal-seeking or anticipatory approach with cyclic return. Activity rises toward an available but unreached state and recurs in cycles until the state is reached or released.
It represents an opaque registry entry or named symbol. The registry records only its identifier and no other field.
It represents a discrepancy or prediction-error signal. It rises when a unit’s own output diverges from what its group expects, and it fades exponentially once the gap is closed in either direction.
It represents a homeostasis or satisfaction signal. It stays low and steady while supply meets demand, renews when attended to, and drops when a deficit appears.
It represents a saturating response. Output rises steeply at first and then flattens toward an asymptotic level it never exceeds.
It represents a threshold switch or step activation. Nothing visible happens while a drive grows, but once it crosses a set value the output jumps abruptly to a new level.
It represents an opaque registry entry or named symbol. Only an identifier is recorded, with no other fields.
It represents loss of damping or growing oscillatory instability. After small knocks, the output takes longer to settle and its wobble grows as the knob is turned.
It represents random telegraph or bistable stochastic switching. The output hops irregularly between two levels and stays at each level for a while.
It represents a boundary-threat or edge-violation alarm. Activity spikes when the inside/outside boundary is pushed on, then fades exponentially after the boundary is restored.

It represents a leaky integrator or accumulator. Output climbs while input is on and decays by a fixed fraction each step when input stops, so brief repeated inputs pile up.

-----

PROPOSED burst/relaxation source: it detects or generates irregular short bursts separated by quiet intervals, with the quiet time shrinking as the knob increases burst rate. Action is to trigger bursts; validation is the monotonic quiet-shortening with knob setting.

PROPOSED shape/constraint-strain signal: it rises when a running process is forced away from its own form and decays exponentially once the form is restored. It detects distortion, drives restoration, and is validated by the fade after restoration.

PROPOSED expectation-gap/error signal: it tracks divergence between a unit’s output and the output its group expects. It drives gap closure in either direction, and exponential fade validates that the mismatch has been resolved.
PROPOSED opaque registry entry: ◭ is bound to an identifier but has no recorded behavior, input, action, or validation. Function is unknown; only the registry binding is traceable.
PROPOSED opaque registry entry: ◰ appears only as an identifier-bound glyph with no other fields. Its detection/action/validation cannot be inferred; mark unknown.
PROPOSED opaque registry entry: ◬ is an identifier-linked registry glyph with no functional fields. It is a bare handle/type tag at most; function unknown.
PROPOSED opaque registry entry: ◱ is recorded only beside an identifier. No pattern or fields give a readable function; mark unknown.

PROPOSED damping-loss/instability signal: after each knock, settling time lengthens and wobble grows as the knob turns. It detects reduced damping/margin and drives a damping adjustment; validation is restored settling.

PROPOSED composite key: ◳ is a lookup key whose value is a list of three other glyphs, so it represents a three-part bundle/composition. No standalone detector/action/validation is recorded; function depends on the referenced glyphs.
PROPOSED composite key: ◴ maps to a list of three glyphs and thus denotes a grouped/composite signal. The group’s function is unknown without the referenced glyphs; no other field is traceable.

PROPOSED saturating response: output rises steeply with input then asymptotically flattens toward a cap. It detects input magnitude and drives a bounded output; validation is the plateau it never passes.

PROPOSED leaky integrator/accumulator: output climbs while input is on and decays by a fixed fraction per step when input stops, so brief repeated inputs pile up. It integrates events with leakage; validation is the fixed fractional decay.

PROPOSED supply-demand/homeostatic signal: low steady activity persists while supply meets demand, renews under attention (resonant class), and drops on deficit. It detects balance and drives renewal/attention; validation is the drop when deficit appears.
PROPOSED opaque registry entry: ◮ is identifier-bound with no other registry field. No functional reading is available; mark unknown.

PROPOSED coherence/invariant signal: very slow-decaying activity is present while system parts remain mutually consistent, and it does not fade on its own (immortal class). It detects consistency and maintains it; validation is persistence without decay.

PROPOSED bistable/telegraph signal: output hops irregularly between two levels and dwells at each for a while. It represents a two-state process with irregular transitions; action/validation are only the observed dwell/switch pattern.

PROPOSED bifurcation/symmetry-breaking detector: as the knob is slowly turned, one resting level splits into two stable levels. It detects emergence of multistability and drives parameter change; validation is the two settle points.

PROPOSED link-loss/reconnection signal: activity follows disappearance of a long-standing connection and returns in cyclical waves until the missing link is re-mapped. It detects broken coupling and drives remapping; validation is cessation of waves.

PROPOSED unmet-availability/goal signal: activity rises toward an available-but-unreached state and cycles until the state is reached or let go. It detects an unclosed gap and drives approach/release; validation is cycle cessation.

PROPOSED hysteresis/Schmitt trigger: output switches on at one knob setting and off only at a lower setting. It detects threshold crossing with memory and drives a latch; validation is the separated up/down thresholds.
PROPOSED opaque registry entry: ◲ appears only beside an identifier with no other field. No detector/action/validation can be read; mark unknown.

PROPOSED anticipated-loss/threat signal: activity rises when something held is projected to be reduced in the future and stays up while the projection persists. It fades exponentially at rate 0.7 once the projection is dealt with; validation is that fade.

PROPOSED hidden-threshold detector: nothing visible changes while a drive grows, then output switches abruptly once the drive passes a set value. It detects threshold crossing and drives a discrete state change; validation is the abrupt switch.

PROPOSED boundary-stress/contact signal: activity spikes when the inside/outside edge is pushed on, with fast rise and exponential fade after the edge is restored. It detects boundary violation and drives restoration; validation is the fade.

-----
PROPOSED: a threshold/step switch. The glyph marks a hidden drive that crosses a setpoint, then causes an abrupt discrete output jump; it detects threshold crossing and triggers a state change.

PROPOSED: a homeostatic/baseline maintenance state. It represents low steady activity while supply matches demand, renewing under attention and dropping under deficit; it keeps the system near baseline.
PROPOSED: a bare registry reference/placeholder. It records only an identifier link and no other field, so it points to identity but supplies no further semantics; unknown fields stay unknown.
PROPOSED: a leaky integrator/accumulator. It sums input while on and loses a fixed fraction per step when input stops, so brief repeated inputs pile up; it accumulates and decays.
PROPOSED: a boundary-perturbation sensor. It spikes when the inside/outside edge is stressed and fades exponentially after restoration; it detects boundary disturbance.
PROPOSED: a persistent coherence/consistency state. It stays present while parts remain mutually consistent and does not fade on its own, marking a long-lived invariant or order parameter.
PROPOSED: a bare registry reference/placeholder. It is an identifier-only entry with no other recorded field, so it does lookup/identity pointing only.
PROPOSED: a pitchfork bifurcation/symmetry-breaking point. As the control knob changes, one resting level splits into two possible stable levels; it marks the onset of bistability.
PROPOSED: a composite lookup entry. Its key maps to an ordered list of three glyphs and no other field, so it encodes a grouped sequence/recipe rather than a single state.
PROPOSED: a cyclic pursuit of an available-but-unreached state. Activity rises toward that state and repeats in cycles until it is reached or released; it drives goal-seeking/return cycles.
PROPOSED: a bare registry reference/placeholder. It records only an identifier link and no other field, so it indicates identity without adding semantics.

PROPOSED: an anticipatory loss/threat signal. It rises when something held is projected to be reduced, stays up while the projection persists, and fades exponentially at rate 0.7 once resolved; it tracks expected future loss.
PROPOSED: a bare registry reference/placeholder. It is an identifier-only registry entry with no other field, so it points but does not further specify.

PROPOSED: a discrepancy/prediction-error signal. It rises when a unit’s own output diverges from what its group expects, then fades once the gap is closed in either direction; it detects role/expectation mismatch.
PROPOSED: a bare registry reference/placeholder. It records only an identifier link and no other field, so it is an identity pointer with unknown extra semantics.
PROPOSED: random bistable switching/metastability. The output hops irregularly between two levels and dwells at each for a while; it represents noisy two-state metastable behavior.
PROPOSED: hysteresis/latching with memory. The up-switch and down-switch occur at different knob settings, so the output depends on history; it implements a threshold with memory.
PROPOSED: loss of damping/approach to instability. After knocks, settling takes longer and wobble grows as the knob is turned; it marks a system moving toward oscillatory instability.
PROPOSED: a loss/reconnection search cycle. Activity follows a vanished long-standing connection and returns in waves until the missing link is re-mapped; it drives cyclical remapping after loss.
PROPOSED: a composite lookup entry. Its key maps to an ordered list of three glyphs and no other field, so it encodes a grouped sequence/recipe.
PROPOSED: a stochastic burst generator. Long quiet stretches are broken by irregular short bursts, and quiet intervals shorten as the knob is turned; it represents increasing random-event rate.
PROPOSED: a deformation/strain signal. Activity tracks a running process forced out of its own shape and fades after the shape is restored; it detects shape/process deformation.
PROPOSED: a bare registry reference/placeholder. It records only an identifier link and no other field, so it points to identity without additional semantics.

PROPOSED: a saturating response. Output rises steeply at first and then flattens toward a ceiling it never passes; it represents bounded/saturating input-output behavior.

-----
≈ represents a homeostatic supply–demand balance: a low, steady state that is renewed by attention and falls when a deficit appears. It maintains equilibrium rather than driving large changes.
◲ is a bare registry reference/opaque identifier. It has no recorded behavior beyond being registered and looked up; it simply names or points to something else.
⎺ represents a persistent consistency invariant or system-integrity constraint. It stays active while the parts remain mutually consistent and does not decay on its own.
◳ is a lookup key mapped to a three-glyph list. It acts as a structured/composite reference whose lookup returns those three glyphs.
⌠ represents a saturating response or diminishing-returns curve. It rises quickly at first and then levels off at a ceiling it never exceeds.

⟍ represents anticipatory loss/anxiety about a held thing being reduced in the future. It rises with that projection, stays elevated while the projection persists, and fades exponentially once the projection is resolved.
⎍ represents a threshold trigger or step function. Nothing changes while the drive builds, then the output switches abruptly once the drive crosses a set value.
◮ is a bare registry reference/opaque identifier. It records only registration/lookup identity, not intrinsic behavior.
◰ is a bare registry reference/opaque identifier. It serves as a registered pointer/name with no other recorded fields.
⌁ represents intermittent bursting or irregular pulse activity. Quiet periods are interrupted by short bursts, and the control knob shortens the quiet stretches.
⌇ represents growing underdamped oscillation/instability. After a knock, the response wobbles more and takes longer to settle as the control knob is turned.
⟍ represents a social expectation-gap signal, such as guilt or norm-deviation detection. It rises when a unit’s output diverges from what its group expects, and fades once the gap is closed.
⌒ represents a leaky integrator. It accumulates input while the input is on and decays by a fixed fraction each step after input stops, so repeated brief inputs pile up.
⦚ represents bistable/noisy switching between two levels. It hops irregularly between two states and stays in each for a while.
◭ is a bare registry reference/opaque identifier. It has only a registered identity and no other recorded field.
◱ is a bare registry reference/opaque identifier. It functions as a registered name/pointer without additional metadata.
∽ represents a loss/separation response to a long-standing connection disappearing. It comes in cyclical waves until the missing link is re-mapped.
∽ represents longing/craving toward an available but unreached state. It cycles until the state is reached or released.
◬ is a bare registry reference/opaque identifier. It records registration identity only and has no intrinsic behavior.
⟍ represents strain/stress from a process being forced out of its own shape. It tracks the distortion and fades exponentially once the shape is restored.
◴ is a lookup key mapped to a three-glyph list. It acts as a structured/composite lookup entry returning those three glyphs.
⟍ represents boundary-threat/defensive alarm. It spikes when the inside/outside edge is pushed, rises fast, and fades after the boundary is restored.
⎎ represents hysteresis. Turning a knob up switches the output at one setting, while turning it back down switches it only at a lower setting.

⋔ represents a bifurcation/pitchfork split. As a control knob is slowly turned, one resting level splits into two possible stable levels.

UNKNOWN. The registry gives only a glyph beside an unshown identifier and no other field, so no input/output, action, or validation can be read. PROPOSED: it is an opaque registry key/reference only.
PROPOSED: a saturating transfer function. It detects increasing input, drives output up steeply at first, then limits/clamps it below a fixed asymptote; validation is monotonic rise to a plateau.

PROPOSED: a supply-demand balance/homeostasis monitor. It stays low while supply meets demand, renews when attended as a resonant maintenance process, and drops when a deficit appears; action is replenishment/attention.
UNKNOWN. Only the glyph and an unshown registry identifier are present, with no observable pattern or fields. PROPOSED: an opaque registry entry with no readable function.
UNKNOWN. The registry record gives no behavior, action, or validation data. PROPOSED: a bare key/reference whose function cannot be assigned from this packet.

PROPOSED: a deformation/deviation detector. It reads activity proportional to a running process being forced out of its own shape, then fades exponentially once shape is restored; action is restore/correct.

PROPOSED: a stability-margin/damping monitor. It detects increasing settling time and growing wobble after small knocks as a knob is turned; action is reduce gain or restore damping, validated by faster settling.
UNKNOWN. The registry records only the glyph beside an unshown identifier. PROPOSED: an opaque entry; no functional read is possible without the identifier or another field.

PROPOSED: a mismatch detector between a unit’s own output and its group’s expected output. Activity rises with divergence and fades exponentially when the gap closes in either direction; action is correction/alignment.
PROPOSED: an unmet-availability drive. It rises toward a state that is available but not reached, cycling until the state is attained or released; action is repeated approach, validated by cessation.
PROPOSED: a threshold switch/comparator. It hides gradual drive growth until a set value is crossed, then switches abruptly to a new output level; action is trigger/step, validated at the threshold.
UNKNOWN. Only an unshown identifier and no other registry field are given. PROPOSED: an opaque registry key; its function cannot be read.
UNKNOWN. The glyph appears only as a registry entry with no behavior or fields shown. PROPOSED: a reference/key only, not enough to assign a function.

PROPOSED: a consistency/invariant monitor. It persists with very slow decay while parts remain mutually consistent and does not fade on its own; action is preserve consistency, validated by persistence until externally changed.

PROPOSED: a composite/dispatcher key that expands to three subglyphs. It would route or compose three subfunctions, but the subglyph identities and any validation are not shown; function remains partly UNKNOWN.

PROPOSED: a leaky integrator/accumulator. Output climbs while input is on and decays by a fixed fraction per step when input stops; brief repeated inputs pile up, validated by accumulation and fractional decay.
PROPOSED: an irregular bistable toggle. Output hops between two levels at irregular moments and dwells at each level; action is state switching, validated by two-level dwell behavior.
PROPOSED: a bifurcation detector/mode split. As a control parameter is slowly turned, one resting level splits into two stable resting levels; action is mode selection, validated by the split.

PROPOSED: a composite lookup key mapping to three other glyphs, like a dispatcher/composition. It would invoke or aggregate three subprocesses, but which three and what validation applies are UNKNOWN.

PROPOSED: an anticipated-loss/looming-deficit detector. Activity rises when a held thing is projected to be reduced in the future, stays up while the projection persists, and fades exponentially at rate 0.7 once dealt with; action is protective/preventive.
PROPOSED: a boundary-breach/pressure detector. It spikes when the inside/outside edge is pushed on, with fast rise and exponential fade after restoration; action is boundary defense/restoration.

PROPOSED: a burst generator driven by accumulated threshold crossing. Long quiet stretches are broken by short irregular bursts, and turning a knob shortens the quiet periods; action is emit bursts, validated by rate change.

PROPOSED: a lost-connection detector plus remapping process. Activity follows disappearance of a long-standing link and returns in cyclical waves until the missing link is re-mapped; action is search/reconnect.

PROPOSED: a hysteresis/Schmitt-trigger function. Turning a knob up switches at one setting, but turning it down switches back only at a lower setting; action is latched switching, validated by asymmetric thresholds.

PROPOSED: ⟍ here is a projected-depletion/error signal. It detects a held quantity projected to fall, drives preparatory correction, and stays active while the projection persists; validation is exponential fade at rate 0.7 once resolved.

PROPOSED: ◱ is an opaque registry reference token. It detects an identifier’s presence and drives lookup/routing to its binding; validation is registry membership. No other field is recorded, so the bound content is unknown.

PROPOSED: ◮ is also an opaque registry reference token. It detects an identifier and drives lookup/routing; validation is presence in the registry. The chain breaks at what the identifier denotes, so deeper function is unknown.
PROPOSED: ◬ is an opaque registry entry marker/reference. It detects a bound identifier and drives lookup/routing; validation is registry presence. Beyond that reference role, no payload is readable.

PROPOSED: ≈ is a supply-demand balance/homeostasis signal. It detects supply meeting demand, drives maintenance or renewed attention, and drops when a deficit appears; validation is low steady activity under matched supply.

PROPOSED: ∽ here is an unresolved-missing-link signal. It detects loss of a long-standing connection, drives cyclical re-mapping/search, and returns in waves until the link is re-mapped; validation is cessation after remapping.

PROPOSED: ⌇ is a damping-loss/instability detector. It detects increasing settling time and growing wobble after small knocks as the knob rises, and drives gain reduction or damping correction; validation is shorter settling and smaller wobble.

PROPOSED: ◳ is a composite lookup key/alias. It detects its key and expands to a list of three other glyphs, driving three-way dispatch or subfunction lookup; validation is the table value. The three subglyphs are unknown here.

PROPOSED: ◴ is a composite dispatch key. It detects its key and expands into three glyphs, driving lookup to those three subfunctions; validation is the recorded value list. The actual three glyphs are not shown, so that part is unknown.

PROPOSED: ◲ is an opaque registry reference token. It detects an identifier and drives lookup/routing to the bound target; validation is registry presence. No other fields means no further function is readable.

PROPOSED: ⌁ is a threshold-burst/relaxation source. It detects accumulated drive and emits short irregular bursts, with quiet stretches shortening as the knob increases; validation is the burst/quiet timing pattern.

PROPOSED: ∽ here is an unattained-available-state signal. It detects a reachable but not-yet-reached state, drives cyclical approach/retry, and repeats until the state is reached or released; validation is cycle termination by reach or letting go.
PROPOSED: ⌠ is a saturating response/limiter. It detects input and drives output steeply at first, then flattens toward a bound it never passes; validation is the plateau behavior.
PROPOSED: ◭ is an opaque registry token/reference. It detects an identifier and drives lookup/routing; validation is registry membership. The pattern supplies no payload beyond that reference role.

PROPOSED: ⟍ here is a shape/deformation mismatch detector. It detects a running process being forced out of its own shape, drives restoration of that shape, and fades exponentially after restoration; validation is the fade once shape is restored.

PROPOSED: ⟍ here is a boundary-breach detector. It detects pressure on an inside/outside edge, drives boundary restoration, and shows fast rise then exponential fade after the edge is restored; validation is fade after restoration.

PROPOSED: ⎎ is a hysteresis switch/comparator. It detects the knob level with memory, switching output at one setting upward and back only at a lower setting downward; validation is the separated switch thresholds.

PROPOSED: ⦚ is a bistable random-dwell latch. It holds two output levels and hops between them at irregular moments, staying at each for a while; validation is the dwell-and-toggle pattern. The trigger source is unknown.

PROPOSED: ⟍ here is an expectation-gap detector. It detects divergence between a unit’s own output and the output its group expects, drives closure of the gap in either direction, and fades exponentially once closed; validation is the fade after gap closure.

PROPOSED: ⎺ is a consistency/coherence baseline signal. It detects mutual consistency among parts, drives maintenance of coupling, and persists without fading on its own; validation is the immortal-class slow-decaying activity while consistency holds.
PROPOSED: ⎍ is a threshold switch. It detects a growing drive crossing a set value and drives an abrupt output step; validation is no visible change before threshold and a switch after it.
PROPOSED: ◰ is an opaque registry token/reference. It detects an identifier and drives lookup/routing; validation is registry presence. No other recorded field means its deeper meaning is unknown.

PROPOSED: ⋔ is a bifurcation/symmetry-breaking detector. As the knob crosses a critical region, one resting level splits into two stable settling levels; it detects the split and drives selection or latching into one branch. Validation is the appearance of two distinct stable rest levels.

PROPOSED: ⌒ is a leaky integrator/accumulator. It detects input-on periods, climbs while input is present, and decays by a fixed fraction each step after input stops; brief repeated inputs summate. Validation is the fixed fractional slide back and pile-up of repeated pulses.

-----

⟍ reads as a mismatch/error transient: activity rises when actual output diverges from expected output and fades exponentially once the gap closes. It functions as a discrepancy alarm that motivates correction and then clears.
⎍ reads as a threshold/step detector: nothing visible happens until a drive crosses a set value, then output switches abruptly. It functions as an all-or-none trigger.
◮ is an opaque registry entry: it marks an identifier with no readable fields. It functions as an unknown handle—do not infer properties; probe or mark unknown.
⌠ reads as a saturating response: steep rise at first, then flattening toward a ceiling it never passes. It functions as a bounded input-output map that prevents unbounded output.
⟍ here reads as a boundary-violation transient: activity spikes when an inside/outside edge is pushed, then fades exponentially after restoration. It functions as a boundary-integrity alarm.
◱ is an opaque registry entry with no other fields. It functions as a registered-but-unspecified referent/placeholder, so treat it as unknown rather than assigning attributes.

⎺ reads as a non-decaying coherence/invariant signal: it persists while parts stay mutually consistent and does not fade on its own. It functions as an integrity/binding flag that can sustain consistency.
⌁ reads as a burst generator: long quiet periods broken by irregular bursts, with quiet periods shortening as a rate knob is turned. It functions as a controllable sporadic-event source.
≈ reads as a renewable steady-state resource/satiation signal: low steady activity when supply meets demand, renews under attention, drops on deficit. It functions as a supply-demand balance monitor.
